summary: Cursor exposes a live preToolUse array with matchers; three adapters are already wired, including a Shell-matcher git advisory built on the shared hard-rule engine — the dispatch gap is wiring, not platform.

cursor/post-tool-use.mjs is a never-blocking multiplexed proxy: Shell to dispatch audit, Write to post-edit quality; hung dispatches produce no post event, so audit-only detects nothing for the main failure class.

Smallest adapter is a translation shim over the 106-line Claude preflight, exactly as task-dispatch-guard.mjs already translates Claude envelopes to Cursor's permission shape; shared library and DISPATCH_SHAPES reused unchanged.

Cursor block shape is {permission:'deny', user_message, agent_message} + exit 2; advisory shape is {permission:'allow', agent_message}; hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext is also parsed but the two dispatch-adjacent shims prefer translation.

NEW DEFECT: DISPATCH_SHAPES codex entry requires -p|--print after 'codex exec', which the real dispatch shape lacks; both documented codex commands produce NO-MATCH, so codex hard rules and audit never fire, while the correct codex shape lives only in HEADLESS_DISPATCH_SHAPES.
Cost table: preToolUse preflight = zero latency, prevents the whole dispatch, covers hangs; postToolUse audit = full dispatch cost, prevents nothing, blind to hangs.
git-preflight-advisory.mjs proves the shared evaluate/readHardRules engine runs unmodified on Cursor and accepts bash/exec/shell payloads with workspace_roots[0] root resolution.
